catalysts: New multipurpose/pulp and auto-carrier capacity continues converting into revenue without margin dilution.
Special-shipping TCE stays above the 2025 run-rate and high-value equipment/auto exports remain resilient.
Semi-submersible/offshore-wind project pipeline exits the current project-window softness.
Fleet expansion is funded without material deterioration in balance-sheet quality or cash conversion.
kill_thesis: Normalized attributable earnings fall below roughly RMB2.0bn without a temporary explanation.
Fleet TCE and gross margin decline together while leased-capacity costs remain elevated.
Auto-export or high-value equipment demand normalizes faster than new fleet capacity can be absorbed.
Operating cash flow materially decouples from reported profit for a sustained period.
At prices materially above base value without commensurate earnings upgrades, valuation itself remains a rejection gate.

records.kill_thesis: Reject D2 promotion if balance-sheet, cash-conversion or normalized-return evidence does not support the defensive label.

catalysts: 207 H1 new ship orders and subsequent orders convert into high-margin deliveries without execution slippage.
High-value tanker/container/VLAC mix sustains H1 margin improvement.
New yard/engine capacity reaches high utilization without cost overruns.
Contract liabilities continue converting into revenue while debt growth moderates.
kill_thesis: New-build price/margin cycle rolls over before the expanded capacity reaches mature utilization.
Order cancellations, delivery delays or raw-material/FX cost pressure reduce normalized margins materially.
Debt and finance expense grow faster than project earnings and customer advances.
Capex remains structurally above operating cash generation after the current expansion phase.
At prices requiring the bull case to justify value, valuation remains a standing rejection gate.
